QuestionStmt.S:
The probability distribution of a discrete random variable $X$ is:

$$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|c|c|}
\hline
X & 0 & 1 & 2 & 3 & 4 \\
\hline
P(X=x) & 2k & k & 2k & 4k & k \\
\hline
\end{array}$$

If $a = P(X < 3)$ and $b = P(2 \leq X < 4)$, then

Solution.S:
Sum of probabilities: $2k + k + 2k + 4k + k = 10k = 1 \Rightarrow k = 0.1$.

$a = P(X < 3) = P(X=0) + P(X=1) + P(X=2) = 2k + k + 2k = 5k = 0.5$.

$b = P(2 \leq X < 4) = P(X=2) + P(X=3) = 2k + 4k = 6k = 0.6$.

Thus $a = 0.5$, $b = 0.6$, so $a < b$.

Hence correct option is C: $a < b$.
